comment: What must not silently disappear from ghfactory. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces — each one is a rule whose loss would be invisible until it caused the failure it exists to prevent. `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run of the ladder.

prose.rationale: The one rule. Every competing AI workflow generator generates and hopes; the differentiator is not the generation but the honesty about what was proven. Lose this line and ghfactory becomes another tool that says 'done' about a workflow nobody ran.
Rungs 0-2 prove refs are real and the YAML is clean. Only a green CI run proves it works. Conflating the two is exactly the failure this skill was built against.

prose.pattern: never emit an action ref you have not resolved
prose.rationale: Measured: actionlint caught six defect classes on a deliberately broken workflow and missed both `actions/checkout@v99` and `actions/setup-nodejs@v4`. No linter checks that an action exists. If ghfactory stops resolving, nothing else in the toolchain will notice a hallucinated action.

prose.pattern: staleness is invisible to every linter
prose.rationale: A hand-written fixture pinning actions/checkout@v5 passed actionlint AND zizmor completely clean while two majors behind. Published research puts the typical workflow 7+ months behind. Existence is not currency, and only ghfactory reports the difference.

`${{ }}` is textual substitution performed before the shell sees the string, so an attacker-controlled PR title is source code, not an argument. This is the most common real vulnerability in real workflows.

prose.pattern: never silently overwrite an existing workflow
prose.rationale: A workflow file is frequently load-bearing for merges. Overwriting one without showing the diff can break every open PR in the repo at once.

prose.pattern: recommend against it\s*\n?\s*until the check has gone green once
prose.rationale: A required check that never passes blocks every future merge — a repo-wide outage produced by a helpful default. The check must be observed green before it gates anything.

The brand lives in press/brand/tokens.json and nowhere else. Hand-writing a masthead recreates precisely the drift press exists to end — this brand was previously eight hand-ported copies across four repos with five names for the same orange.
Detection reads `gh secret list` to know what exists. A secret VALUE entering the process or the transcript would turn a convenience feature into a credential leak.

prose.pattern: never ask about anything in that table
prose.rationale: Two questions maximum is achievable only because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes every other generator feel like a form.

_baseline_comment: Pinned against the real files the ladder was developed against, and the real defect classes the real tools reported on them. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, no spend.

baseline.rationale: Byte-exact, deliberately — the same reason it is right for shipflow's rendered workflow and press's emitted regions: the generated bytes ARE the contract. One changed character changes how every workflow ghfactory has ever written looks. Also asserts the body is entirely comment lines, which caught a real bug during development: renderRegion comments only the markers, so a bare body spliced box-drawing into the document and produced YAML that could not parse.

Two-sided: the good fixture must parse cleanly and the broken one must still carry every defect class it was frozen for — dead ref, nonexistent action, misspelled input, template injection, deprecated command. A one-sided baseline goes green the day someone weakens a checker. Also pins with:-key attribution, because mis-attributing them would make input validation vacuous: it would check an empty key list and always pass.

baseline.update_command: gh api -X GET repos/github/codeql-action/contents/analyze/action.yml -f ref=<sha> --jq .content | base64 -d > evals/baseline/inputs-codeql-analyze.yml
baseline.rationale: Real action.yml files at the SHAs this repo pins, not synthetic ones. Two-sided because each side fails differently: codeql-analyze's `wait-for-processing` is required-WITH-default and must NOT be reported missing — the false positive that made rung 0 red on every correct CodeQL workflow, and a rung nobody can get green is a rung people learn to ignore. paths-filter's `filters` is required with NO default and must still be reported, or the fix has quietly turned input checking off rather than corrected it.

collectUses is the front door of rung 0. If it silently matched nothing, every downstream check would report 'all clean' having verified zero actions — the exact way a gate turns decorative. The floor asserts it finds real references across this repo's own workflows, so a parser regression goes red instead of quiet.
